To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human intestinal microbiome harbours between 1500 and 1600 prevalent bacterial species, each individual harbours at least 160 of them, which are shared among the majority of the individuals, and that these species have a minimal set of 1267 genes in common.
the human gut microbiota harbours a very large number of bacterial species that share many functions and that the majority of genes in the microbiota are bacterial.

the human gut microbiota is dominated by a small number of species, each of which carries a large number of genes, and that the entire microbiota is dominated in terms of gene numbers and functions by a small number and fraction of genes, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the human gut microbial gene repertoire and the description of the minimal gut metagene and the minimal gut genome.
the identification and characterization of the genes and gene functions present in the intestinal microbiota of a large cohort of healthy European individuals.
the identification and characterization of a large number of genes that are prevalent in a cohort of European individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have characterized the human gut microbial gene complement, the gut metagenome, in unprecedented depth.
the human gut microbial gene repertoire is huge, largely shared and dominated by the bacteria.
this study has provided a catalogue of the genes that are present in the human gut microbial ecosystem of the cohort.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have characterized the gene content of the gut microbiome in terms of its composition and functions, and that this is largely shared among humans.
the human gut microbiome contains a huge and diverse gene repertoire, which is largely shared among individuals and that this repertoire is dominated by bacterial species.
a large majority of the human gut microbial genes and prevalent bacterial species are shared among individuals, but that the gut microbial genes of an individual are unique.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human intestinal microbial gene catalogue is a valuable resource for understanding the impact of the gut microbiota on human health.
the vast majority of the human intestinal microbial genes are shared between individuals and that the minimal gut metageneome contains a large fraction of these genes.

the human gut microbiota is dominated by a few species, each of which carries a large proportion of all the genes present in the microbiota, and that the microbiota is largely shared among individuals.
